label: first copy step (echo of first token) in long sequences, gated by first-token identity
explanation: Fires almost only at the step just after <DEL>, where the first original token is fed back as input and the model outputs original token 1 (recall_idx==1 holds 94% of activation mass, 90% recall, but only 11% precision on its own). The rate grows sharply with sequence length (none for L<=4, ~0.3% of steps at L=6, largest at L=9). Within that step it is modulated by the identity of the first token (u > v,j > 3 > c,t > 2,o,p,n; the top examples are all u/v/j/t first) and more weakly by the second token being output (d,m,b,h,i,0 raise it; o,e,a,l,z lower it); this graded token dependence is why no boolean predicate gets past F1 ~0.6. A small leftover (~3% of mass) fires on the last original step (orig_idx 8, L=9) and at recall_idx 2. Never fires at t<6, on the delimiter step, or later in the copy phase (recall_idx>=3).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (copy phase: u, j, v, 3; input phase: c, 3, v, o; delimiter step: ) and the token being output (most: d, m, b, h, i, 0; least: 2, q, o, c); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=8, t=8.
